extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in theatre criticism, actors, theatrical historians, and general readers of biographical/critical essays
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating dramatic works and acting performances with attention to characterization, preparation, style, delivery, moral/psychological insight, pacing, and audience fit. The guidance is aimed at critics, practitioners, and informed audiences assessing artistic merit versus popular appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oration effectiveness (sentiments, style, delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: The oration 'in its sentiments, its style, its delivery, was extraordinarily successful.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectiveness arises from alignment of sentiment, literary style, and delivery with audience expectations; rhetorical fervor and popular temper can greatly boost immediate reception even if they overstate literary or philosophical rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of conviction and picturesque vigor
rubrics_metrics.description: The oration 'expressed his honest convictions' and 'with so much picturesque vigor, and those convictions were so generous and so genuinely American, that the popularity of the oration was no matter of wonder.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sincerity of belief and vivid, culturally resonant imagery increase an address's appeal and credibility; authenticity can compensate for rhetorical excesses in popular contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic focus: domestic/psychological drama versus spectacle
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Broker of Bogota' is described as 'a purely domestic drama, a drama of individual and family affections and trials' lacking 'the great passions of patriotism, liberty, ambition, revenge, public spirit and enterprise' and spectacle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a play aims for intimate psychological truth rather than public spectacle; refined, subtle dramas may be artistically superior but less immediately attractive to popular audiences seeking showy scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and attention to minutest details
rubrics_metrics.description: Forrest 'took unwearied pains to perfect himself even to the very minutest details in the representation of the title-rôle.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough role preparation and painstaking attention to small details in gesture, voice, and behavior are criteria of professional workmanship and deepen realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision and economy of performance (no superfluity)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Nothing seemed wanting, nothing seemed superfluous. Every tone, every glance, every gesture, every step, contributed towards shaping out the ideal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideal acting is economical and purposeful: every element should contribute to characterization and meaning. Extraneous action or rhetorical padding detracts from artistic unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nuanced differentiation of similar character-types (portrayal of age)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forrest's 'distinction he always made in his rendering of old age' across Richelieu, Lear, and Febro—each showing different aspects of age: wily craft, broken yet gigantic power, and hale honorable age respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether an actor distinguishes between similar archetypes by adapting manner, energy, and moral tone to the specific character rather than employing a single 'type' across roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of moral passion and stage presence to shape conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Febro's 'scorn and indignation... break out in a paralyzing explosion of gesture and speech' so that 'the broker makes the noble cower and flee before the storm of his angry contempt.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how convincingly an actor uses moral intensity and presence to dominate scenes and generate believable reversals in onstage power dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of pacing: alternating crisis of suspense and fulfilment
rubrics_metrics.description: The performance contained 'the alternating crisis of suspense and fulfilment as the plot proceeds through gloom and gleam of crime and innocence to the last awful climax.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good dramatic construction balances suspense and release; evaluate timing, build-up, and resolution to see if they produce intended emotional effects without melodrama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience fit and accessibility (subtlety vs mass appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece 'required an audience of psychologists, critically interested in the study of human nature, and curious as to its modes of individual manifestation. The general multitude must feel it to be rather dull and tiresome.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider intended audience: subtle, psychologically rich performances may be lauded by critics but fail to engage broader crowds. Assess whether the work successfully reaches its intended demographic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral clarity and dramatic contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: The contrast between Caberero (a brilliant and hardened scoundrel) and Febro (an upright, courteous banker) provides 'a moral lesson of the strongest kind, set in a dramatic picture of the finest art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the ethical or moral framing of characters and whether contrasts are rendered convincingly to produce ethical insight without simplification or caricature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic refinement versus commercial showiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The play 'lacked those showy scenes and exciting points which attract the crowd' and was 'too fine for his average audiences' despite being admired by 'refined and cultivated judges.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance artistic subtlety and commercial viability: note when artistic choices (lack of spectacle, restraint) reduce box-office appeal, and judge whether artistic gains justify smaller popular reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional revelation and inner-life disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A good performance 'puts off the armor of sternness, and lets us into the world of a heart... It has given us a glimpse of his nature... the heart's story... reveals' inner sensibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess an actor's capacity to disclose inner emotional life—moments of vulnerability, interiority, and layered feeling that transform a surface display into a moving, humane portrait.
